findings.claim: The banner-derivation edit inserted mid-function returns into adversarial-runner's selfTest: the swept pins, the banner, and the boolean verdict were unreachable dead code — --self-test always exited 0 printing nothing, silently neutering the battery member and the verified-phase gate behind it
findings.proof: Any regression in lanesFromCheckchecklist parsing, the bundle contract (including the dead-verifier clause this wave added), or the aggregation seam pushes onto the failures array — but the only reachable return was laneCases.length (3, truthy), so process.exit(selfTest() ? 0 : 1) exited 0 and npm run selftest stayed green while the runner printed nothing. Pre-fix the same path printed the banner and returned a real boolean; the commit's 'all GREEN' claim was vacuous for the runner.

findings.claim: The once-per-session destructive key lets the client spend the single ask on the cheapest classified danger, suppressing facts for every other destructive command for 30 minutes
findings.dedupKey: the once-per-session destructive key lets the client spend the single ask on the cheapest classified danger, suppressing facts for every other destructive command for 30 minutes
findings.justification: This is the spec's stated shape (issue #14: 'first destructive command per session'), confirmed in the grilling tree; the 30-minute TTL bounds the window, the demand names the specific danger it asked about, and the alternative (per-danger-class asking) is exactly what the spec rejected. The sequencing attack is real but bounded: one deliberate ask per session is the intended friction budget, and the bypass class (the laws that matter most) still refuses EVERY time.
